pages.text:
Week 5 — HTTP Caching (slides).

A cache stores a response so a repeat request need not reach the origin server. Cache-Control: max-age=N says the response is fresh for N seconds; within that time the cache serves it without contacting the origin. no-store forbids caching altogether.
A stale response is not necessarily wrong. The cache can revalidate it, asking the origin whether it changed.

Lab 5 — Conditional requests.

The origin sends an ETag, an identifier for the version of the response. On revalidation the client sends If-None-Match with that ETag. If the resource is unchanged the origin replies 304 Not Modified with no body, saving bandwidth; otherwise it replies 200 with the new body.

Task: use curl to fetch a resource twice and observe the 304.

required_facts.fact: max-age=N means fresh for N seconds, served without contacting the origin
a stale response is not necessarily wrong and can be revalidated
If-None-Match with the ETag yields 304 Not Modified with no body if unchanged

forbidden_claims.claim: claims a stale response must be discarded
